text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- 1997 budget deficit expected to reach 270 to 280 billion francs, after a 288 billion-franc deficit in 1996, but government still expects France to meet Maastricht treaty criteria and bring budget deficit down to three percent of GDP in 1997.
-- President Jacques Chirac visits Poland, says Poland should join European union by year 2000.
-- BNP posts 1.7 billion franc profit for the first half, thanks to its international activity and financial markets operations.
-- Air France Europe chairman Christian Blanc could start legal action against pilots who yesterday went on strike without giving the warning required in law.

-- Employers' federation says an eight-billion-franc cut in workers' unemployment payroll contributions could be more efficient in boosting employment than current incentive schemes. Unemployment fund Unedic is expected to post a 12 billion franc surplus in 1997.
-- Air France Europe pilots went on strike for increased security checks on luggage aboard planes.
-- Credit Lyonnais workers demonstrate against restructuring plan that involves 5,000 job cuts up to 1998.
-- Wall Street rises but misses record.
